chunks: My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb all narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

On the fifteenth of Sha’bān, a caller calls out from the highest horizon: O those who have come to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (peace be upon him)! Return forgiven and your rewards will be given (to you) by Allāh, your Lord, and by Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family), your Prophet.

key_terms.النِّصْفُ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ: The fifteenth of the month of Sha’bān
key_terms.زَائِرِي الْحُسَيْنِ: Those who perform Ziyārah of al-Ḥusain

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the fifteenth of Sha’bān regarding the Ziyārah of Imam al-Ḥusain?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the unique spiritual status of the 15th of Sha’bān (Laylat al-Bara'at) as a time when divine mercy is specifically extended to pilgrims of Imam al-Husain (a.s.). The 'caller from the highest horizon' signifies a celestial proclamation, reinforcing the belief that visiting the Imam’s shrine on this night secures guaranteed forgiveness and divine acceptance, linking the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt directly to the Prophet’s legacy.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb all narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

On the fifteenth of Sha’bān, a caller calls out from the highest horizon: O those who have come to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)! Return forgiven and your rewards will be given (to you) by Allāh, your Lord, and by Muḥammad (s.a.a.w.), your Prophet.
